analysis_md:
# JKHY — Jack Henry & Associates, Inc.
Engine 5.4.0 run, 2026-10-19. Price $153.19 (nasdaq_quote_api). Market cap (est) $11.036B — in scope under $40B.

All DCF figures below are copied from key_numbers.md / dcf_numbers.json — none are recomputed. Segment, statement and filing figures are quoted from this run's segments.json, statements.json, fundamentals.json and the FY26 earnings release (8-K, August 18, 2026).

## What it is
Core banking technology for US community and regional banks and credit unions — the smallest of the Big Three core providers (Jack Henry vs Fiserv and FIS). FY26 revenue $2,544,339,000 (+7.12% YoY) by segment (segments.json): Payments $936,006,000 (36.8% of revenue, +7.2% YoY), Core $768,452,000 (30.2%, +4.9%), Complementary $752,214,000 (29.6%, +8.3%), Corporate Services $87,667,000 (3.4%, +18.3%). Products include the Jack Henry Core and Symitar core platforms, Banno digital banking and Payrailz payments. FY26 was a record sales year: 58 competitive core wins, 14 at institutions with more than $1B in assets. FY27 guidance (earnings release): revenue $2,684–2,709M (+5.5–6.5% GAAP), operating margin 24.5–24.7%, EPS $7.33–7.38. Headcount 7,300 (profile.json).

## Owner's earnings
**FY2026 (10-K via EDGAR, from financials_history.csv):** operating cash flow $761,960,000; capex $67,103,000 (PaymentsToAcquirePropertyPlantAndEquipment); SBC $32,460,000 (always a real cost, 4.3% of OCF).
- **Conservative owner's earnings FY2026: $662,397,000 = $9.19/share** (key_numbers.md: latest FY OE/share $9.19, latest FY OE total $662.4M)
- Maintenance version (NI + D&A − min(capex, D&A) − ΔNWC, from financials_history.csv): $465,703,000 — materially below the conservative figure because OCF runs far ahead of net income plus depreciation at this business (advance-collected support/processing fees and deferred-revenue build are inside OCF). The OCF-based conservative figure is the method's base series and is used throughout; the maintenance gap is a business-model feature (customers prepay), not a one-off, and it cuts in the conservative direction for the maintenance definition only.
- OE positive 5 of the last 5 fiscal years. Net debt (latest) $27.9M — 0.05x normalized OE (diagnostics). Buybacks were $448,173,000 in FY26 (fundamentals.json); DPS TTM $2.38 with 17 consecutive growth years (fundamentals.json).

**Base used = normalized owner's earnings, median of the last 3 fiscal years: $7.66/share** (base_source: median_of_last_3_fy_oe_per_share). The three legs are FY24 $6.59, FY25 $7.66 and FY26 $9.19 per share (financials_history.csv) — the median is the FY25 print, so the base sits well below what FY26 already delivered; that conservatism is deliberate in the method and is quantified in the method range below. FY26 ended 3.6 months ago (months since FY end, key_numbers.md), so the base is not stale: ttm.py cannot compute a post-FY TTM (it exits non-zero — no 10-Q has been filed since the 2026-06-30 fiscal year end), and the FY26 year is itself the freshest twelve months available.

### Method limit — capitalized software development is NOT in the scored capex (read this before quoting the tier)
The engine's capex leg is the PP&E tag only. Jack Henry separately capitalizes software development, an investing cash outflow under the tag PaymentsToDevelopSoftware of $167,175,000 in FY24, $172,445,000 in FY25 and $184,243,000 in FY26 (statements.json line "Purchases of intangibles / software"; fundamentals.json capex_intangibles — verified against EDGAR companyfacts as entirely PaymentsToDevelopSoftware for these years). That is roughly three times the PP&E capex deducted in each base year, it is recurring, and it is rising — it is the cash cost of building the product the moat rests on. The scored OE, base and IRR therefore exclude a real maintenance cost on the order of a quarter of the printed OE base, and the printed weighted IRR of 10.07% is an **upper bound**: a software-inclusive owner's-earnings base would be materially lower and the IRR with it. No override was used to patch this: the engine's capex definition is a system-wide method choice applied identically to every software name in the sweep (the same treatment was noted, not overridden, at ZS), overrides only fill missing periods and cannot replace a filed figure, and redefining the capex leg is a main-agent decision. Confidence is graded **low** for this reason as well as the scenario spread, and the caveat is carried in the one-liner so it travels with the ranking.

## Moat: 7/10 — strong
Justification: Mission-critical core processing with very high switching costs and a decade of ROIC proxy at 19–25% (23.5% in FY26), but the smallest of the Big Three core providers, a structurally shrinking US bank/credit-union client base, and moat maintenance that costs $167–184M/yr of capitalized software development.
- Evidence (fundamentals.json): ROIC proxy (after-tax operating income over equity + debt − cash) printed 19.2–25.2% in every year FY17–FY26 — 19.8% in FY23 and 23.5% in FY26 — never approaching the cost of capital, through COVID and the 2023 regional-bank stress. Management reported ROIC of 23.2% for FY26 in the earnings release. Gross margin ranged 39.5–44.1% over FY17–FY26 (fundamentals.json): it eroded from 44.1% in FY17 to a 39.5% trough in FY21, then recovered to 43.7% in FY26 — near the decade high and the best of the last five years — and operating margin recovered to 25.0% in FY26 from 22.1% in FY24. The margin record is erosion-then-recovery, not an unbroken band; the recovery back to near-decade-highs is itself the pricing-power evidence. A 7 sits on that ROIC record; it is not an 8 because the franchise's served market shrinks structurally and its two rivals out-scale it.
- FOR: Mission-critical core platforms (Jack Henry Core for banks, Symitar for credit unions) — a core conversion is the highest-risk project a bank runs; multi-year contracts, very low churn. Integrated stack raises switching costs with each product (Core, Payments, Complementary, Banno). Record 58 competitive core wins in FY26, 14 over $1B in assets — taking share from Fiserv/FIS. ROIC and margin record above.
- AGAINST: Smallest of the Big Three — Fiserv and FIS have far greater scale and R&D budgets. US bank/credit-union consolidation deletes a customer at every merger; deconversion fees are one-time, the recurring revenue is gone. Moat maintenance is expensive and rising (capitalized software, above). Cloud-native and modular challengers (nCino, Mambu, Temenos, fintech point solutions) unbundle pieces of the stack. Served market grows slowly — revenue CAGR ~7% over 5 years, FY27 guided +5.5–6.5% — and the book is concentrated in US community/regional institutions.
- A 7 gives CAP = 11.1 years: growth holds 2 years, then converges linearly to the 2.5% terminal rate over 11.1 years, 15-year projection.

## DCF — final run (engine 5.4.0, 2026-10-19)
Probabilities 10/25/30/25/10, growth-start offsets −12/−5/0/+5/+12pp vs the blended start, OE multipliers 0.75/0.90/1.00/1.10/1.25 — all defaults, kept because the sanity check below supports them for this company. Blended growth 7.88% (components: rev CAGR 5y 7.67%, rev CAGR 3y 6.99%, latest rev YoY 7.12%, OE/share CAGR 2y 18.16%; share count CAGR −0.48%, growth adj 0.48%).

**Growth-start sanity check (against actual prints and guidance):**
- Base start 7.9% vs prints: FY26 revenue grew 7.12% and Q4 FY26 non-GAAP revenue grew 6.6% (earnings release), while FY27 guidance is revenue +5.5–6.5% and EPS $7.33–7.38. The base start is an OE/share growth rate, not a revenue rate: it sits above the revenue guide on buyback support ($448,173,000 repurchased in FY26; the blend already credits the −0.48%/yr share trend) — and it is applied to the $7.66 median base, which is below the $9.19 FY26 already printed, so the base path's first-year OE/share of $8.27 (dcf_numbers.json paths) remains below the latest actual print. On level, the base case is conservative despite the growth rate.
- Bull start 12.9%: above every revenue print, and defensible only as an OE/share case — FY26 OE/share rose from $7.66 to $9.19 in one year and operating margin expanded from 23.9% (FY25) to 25.0% (FY26) (fundamentals.json), with Q4 processing revenue +7.5% and faster payments +47% (earnings release). It requires that operating leverage and core-win conversions, not revenue acceleration, do the work.
- Super-bull start 19.9%: approximately the OE/share growth FY26 actually printed ($7.66 → $9.19); with the 1.25 OE multiplier it assumes FY26's OCF strength is the new run-rate and compounds. Priced at only 10% probability.
- Bear 2.9% / super bear −4.1%: OCF normalization is a lived precedent here — FY23 OE/share printed $4.29 (financials_history.csv) when OCF dipped. Even the super-bear starting point (0.75x the base) sits above that trough print, so the bear side is firm but not draconian.

| Scenario | Prob | Growth start | OE mult | Story | IV@15 | IRR |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Super bear | 10% | -4.1% | 0.75 | OCF normalization repeats the FY23 dip; consolidation churn bites | $34.56 | 5.02% |
| Bear | 25% | 2.9% | 0.9 | Growth fades toward the low end of guidance; deconversion losses mount | $57.57 | 7.22% |
| Base | 30% | 7.9% | 1.0 | Current trajectory on the median base; buybacks support OE/share | $81.04 | 9.38% |
| Bull | 25% | 12.9% | 1.1 | Operating leverage + core-win conversions repeat FY26's OE/share leverage | $113.05 | 12.06% |
| Super bull | 10% | 19.9% | 1.25 | FY26 OCF strength is the run-rate and compounds | $179.17 | 16.69% |

- **Probability-weighted: IV@15% $88.34 (−42.3% vs price), IV@12% $119.61 (−21.9%), IV@10% $154.82, weighted IRR 10.07%, base-case IRR 9.38%**
- **Tier by numbers: C.** Diagnostics (key_numbers.md): OE yield 5.00%, terminal value 20.8% of IV@15%, scenario spread 5.18x, net debt 0.05x normalized OE, 3.6 months since FY end.
- Hurdle-clearing prices (weighted path): 15% at $88.34, 20% at $60.68, 25% at $45.76 — the $153.19 price clears none of them; even the bull case alone (IV@15 $113.05) sits below the price, and only the 10%-probability super bull ($179.17) exceeds it.

## Flags — every fragility flag resolved
- **CASH_INCLUDES_RESTRICTED** (the only cash tag filed for the latest fiscal year is the combined cash + restricted-cash total; no restricted-cash tag separates it — net debt may be understated): resolved as immaterial either way. The FY26 balance sheet (financials_history.csv) shows combined cash of $12,056,000 against total debt of $40,000,000 (credit facilities drawn $40M at June 30, 2026 vs $0 at June 30, 2025, per the earnings release), giving the printed net debt of $27.9M at 0.05x normalized OE. Even in the worst case — the entire cash line treated as restricted — net debt could not exceed the $40,000,000 gross debt figure, which is still trivial against the OE base. The absence of HIGH_NET_DEBT is safe; no escalation needed.
- **WIDE_SCENARIO_SPREAD** (super-bull IV is 5.2x super-bear IV): the spread is a duration artifact of compounding a −4.1% to +19.9% growth range over an 11.1-year fade on a long-lived franchise, not base uncertainty — OE was positive 5 of the last 5 years and revenue has grown every year in the filed history. Confidence is capped accordingly (graded low, also for the capitalized-software limit above) and the verdict is sized to the bear end.
- **TIER_BAND** (bear-case tier D at 7.22% vs bull-case tier C at 12.06%): sized to the bear end. The band matters less than usual here because the entire band — bear, base and bull — sits below the 15% hurdle at the $153.19 price; no scenario in the band changes the action.

## My thoughts / overlay
- The honest headline is a range, and both ends of it fail the hurdle. On the scored median base: weighted IRR 10.07%, IV@15% $88.34, Tier C. On the most generous defensible base — the latest FY OE/share of $9.19 used directly (exploratory engine run pinned to that base via --base-oe-ps, same moat 7 and probabilities; full generated output committed as dcf_numbers_latest_fy_base.json) — weighted IRR 11.45%, IV@15% $105.99, still Tier C. Method range: Tier C either way, IV@15% $88–106 vs the $153.19 price. And both ends are upper bounds, because neither deducts the $167–184M/yr of capitalized software development detailed above; a software-inclusive run would print lower, toward the bear end.
- Quality is not the debate: ROIC proxy 19–25% for a decade, gross margin 43.7%, operating margin 25.0%, net debt 0.05x normalized OE, $448,173,000 of FY26 buybacks, a 17-year dividend growth record, and record core wins. This is a valuation verdict, not a business verdict — the market is paying $153.19 for a stream the model values at $88–106 at a 15% discount rate.
- Street context (street.json, cache, not scored): consensus Buy, n=15, target $190.56. The gap to this model is the usual one for JKHY — the Street underwrites the franchise premium and mid-single-digit growth at a lower discount rate; at a 10% discount rate the weighted IV is $154.82, essentially the current price, which is another way of saying the price already assumes roughly a 10% required return.
- Watch items: FY27 delivery against the +5.5–6.5% revenue guide (Q4 FY26 GAAP revenue grew only 4.7%, with deconversion revenue inside it); whether capitalized software keeps outgrowing revenue; bank M&A pace (each merger deletes a client and books a one-time deconversion fee); the Jack Henry Platform cloud migration's effect on the Core segment's +4.9% growth, the slowest of the three main segments.

## Final verdict
- **Final tier: C** (weighted IRR 10.07% on the scored median base; method range C on every defensible base, with the printed figure an upper bound for the capitalized-software reason above)
- Confidence: **Low** (WIDE_SCENARIO_SPREAD plus a known, quantified cost excluded from the scored OE by the engine's capex definition)
- One-liner: High-quality core-banking franchise, moat 7/10 — does not clear 15% at $153.19 (weighted IRR 10.1%, IV@15 $88.34; clears 15% only below ~$88) and the scored OE excludes $167-184M/yr of capitalized software development, so the printed IRR is an upper bound.

## Data / enrichment
Enrichment all ran (non-blocking): fundamentals.json (10 annual years, TTM through 2026-06-30), prices.json, segments.json (segment and product revenue tables tie to the consolidated total), statements.json, profile.json (description from the 10-K Item 1, 7,300 employees, no warnings) and street.json (consensus Buy, target $190.56 — a cache file, not scored); reprice.py repriced the scored paths at the last close with no tier change. ttm.py exits non-zero for the reason given under Owner's earnings (no post-FY 10-Q yet) — the median base stands. statements.py carries its standard cross-filing-generation warnings on old captions (notably the capex_intangibles caption across filing generations); none touch the FY24–FY26 OE legs, and the FY22–FY26 capitalized-software series was verified directly against EDGAR companyfacts.
